Democracy Defender Mod Manager (DDMM), release candidate 13: *your mods, your democracy, defended.* It's still an
early build, but it's meant to be usable by anyone, not just developers.

**The DDMM Promise, in brief:** every mod is welcome (DDMM never blocks, blacklists or ranks mods or mod sites),
no account is ever needed on any site, your files stay in a folder you control, it's Apache-2.0 open source
forever, and update checks never run unless you ask.

## Quick start

1. **Download** the right file for you (see the table below).
2. **Run it.** DDMM looks for your Helldivers 2 install automatically. If Steam is in its usual place, there's
   nothing to set up.
3. **Add mods and click Deploy.** Drag in an archive or folder, or click "Add URL" and paste a link.

**Works with AyakaMods, Nexus Mods, ModWorkshop, GameBanana, GitHub, any direct link, or files already on your
disk.** Special love to the AyakaMods community ❤️, one of the best homes for Helldivers 2 modding. Go say hi:
<https://ayakamods.com/games/helldivers-2.119/>.

## Which file do I download?

| You want... | Download |
| --- | --- |
| A normal install on Windows (Start Menu shortcut, uninstaller) | `DDMM-2.0.0-rc.13-windows-x64-setup.exe` |
| Windows without installing anything (unzip and run) | `DDMM-2.0.0-rc.13-windows-x64-portable.zip` |
| Linux: Fedora, Nobara, openSUSE (`dnf`/`zypper`) | `DDMM-2.0.0-rc.13-linux-x86_64.rpm` |
| Linux: Debian, Ubuntu, Mint (`apt`) | `DDMM-2.0.0-rc.13-linux-amd64.deb` |
| Linux: other distros, no install (uses your desktop's graphics libraries) | `DDMM-2.0.0-rc.13-linux-x86_64.AppImage` |
| Linux: Arch/CachyOS, or just the binary (needs WebKitGTK 4.1) | `DDMM-2.0.0-rc.13-linux-x64.tar.gz` |

Linux install commands, the dependencies for each distro, and fixes for a blank window or AppImage/FUSE errors
are in [Installing on Linux](https://katsyk.github.io/DemocracyDefenderModManager/getting-started/linux/).

**One-click install (optional):** also grab the browser extension: `ddmm-extension-chrome-1.0.0.zip`
(Chrome, Edge, Brave) or `ddmm-extension-firefox-1.0.0.zip` (Firefox). See
[One-click install](https://katsyk.github.io/DemocracyDefenderModManager/using/one-click-install/).

Check `SHA256SUMS.txt` if you want to verify your download.

## What's new in 2.0.0-rc.13

### AyakaMods update checks (#59)

- **Updates released on the same day are now caught.** AyakaMods labels each update with its date, so two updates
  on the same day looked identical and DDMM missed the second one. DDMM now also compares when the mod's page was
  last updated.
- **Gentler on the site.** DDMM now checks AyakaMods mods one at a time with a short pause between them. If the
  site turns DDMM away, it waits and tries once more; if the site keeps refusing, DDMM stops asking it for the rest
  of that check and shows a clear reason instead of a bare "403 Forbidden". It never tries to get around the
  site's protection.
- **Clearer errors.** A mod whose page can't be found (removed or moved) now says so plainly, and DDMM's log lists
  every mod whose check failed, with the site, the mod's id and the reason.
- Mods installed with the browser extension now get the same accurate update tracking.
- For mods installed before this release, DDMM allows for a difference between your PC's clock and the site's,
  so a wrong clock doesn't make an up-to-date mod look out of date.

### Smaller fixes

- When the browser is still writing a download under a temporary name, DDMM now waits for it to finish instead of
  installing an empty (0-byte) zip. Unrelated downloads in the same folder don't hold it up.
- Importing a mod that already has DDMM's install record keeps its original install time, so a pending update
  isn't hidden.

Thanks again to @jackiejackie495 for the detailed report and log. o7

**Skipped a few?** rc.10 had important safety fixes, rc.11 fixed mod deletion and rc.12 fixed mod option dropdowns; see the [releases page](https://github.com/katsyk/DemocracyDefenderModManager/releases).

## Known limitations

- **Windows builds are unsigned.** Windows SmartScreen will likely show a warning the first time you run the
  installer or the app. Click **"More info" → "Run anyway"** to continue.
- **The Linux .rpm and .deb are unsigned**, so openSUSE needs `zypper install --allow-unsigned-rpm`.
- **This is still a release candidate.** Expect some rough edges, and please report what you find.
